summary: Elevated first-token latency and intermittent streaming cutouts after model ABI + runtime migration
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (NimbusApps, dedicated) reports significantly longer wait for the first token on chat completions and occasional streaming disconnects following the coordinated model ABI and serving runtime migration on 2026-03-09. Impact is customer-facing: chat flows stall for 2–6 seconds before the first token, and ~1% of sessions see an immediate stream termination (504/502) within first 5s.

Impact:
- Increased TTFB (first-token latency) observed across small and medium prompts; baseline ~80–120ms → observed 2,000–6,000ms.
- Intermittent streaming cutouts resulting in 5xxs for a small subset of sessions.
- Affects conversational UX: typing indicator freezes, client-side timeouts.

Environment:
- Dedicated cluster in us-east-1 assigned to NimbusApps.
- Serving runtime v2.7.0 deployed 2026-03-09 03:10 UTC alongside model pin to redwood/gptx-7b-v2-q4_0 (ABI change applied).
- Router version 1.14.2 with affinity routing and prefetch enabled.

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1. Start a new chat session via /v1/chat/completions using model redwood/gptx-7b-v2-q4_0 with streaming=true and small prompt (~20 tokens).
2. Observe client-side wait until first onDelta event or first token chunk appears.
3. Some sessions return 504/502 within first 5s.

Expected behavior:
- First token emitted within ~100–200ms for small prompts; stable streaming connection for entire session.

Observed behavior:
- First token latency spikes to 2–6s for 70–80% of requests during peak; median increased from 120ms to ~2.3s.
- ~0.8–1.2% sessions abort with 5xx within first 5s.

Recent changes (relevant):
- 2026-03-09 03:10 UTC: Serving runtime v2.7.0 rolled to dedicated cluster; included ABI change to KV cache layout and a kernel selection tweak for Q4 quantized models.
- 2026-03-09 03:15 UTC: Router prefetch policy enabled for low-latency customers; affinity rebalancing applied.

Logs / metrics snippets (support capture):
- Customer-reported session IDs: nimbus-req-5a7c3, nimbus-req-5a7c7, nimbus-req-5a7d1.
- Metrics (cluster: nimbus-dedicated-01, window 03:00–06:00 UTC): first_token_latency p50 120ms -> 2.3s, p95 350ms -> 4.8s.
- Serving logs show transient "cache miss, rehydrate kv" events aligned with slow requests.
- Router logs show occasional 504 routed back from streaming-proxy for connections aged <5s.

Initial triage / investigation notes:
- Verified customer is pinned to Q4 variant and cluster received the v2.7.0 runtime; reproducer built against the same config shows similar elevation in first-token latency.
- Heap and GPU utilization within normal range; no evident OOM.
- Observed increased frequency of cold-KV rehydrates on ABI-swapped models: new ABI requires migration of prefix/KV layout causing synchronous rehydrate path on first request post-upgrade.
- Router prefetch appears to sometimes emit an additional warmup RPC to a fallback path, delaying main request by ~1.2s in some traces.

Hypotheses:
1) ABI change introduced a synchronous migration step on first model invocation which blocks token emission until KV rehydrate completes.
2) Router prefetch/warmup sequence adds a serialized handshake before the primary request reaches serving runtime for pinned customers due to affinity rules.
3) In rare cases a misconfigured health-probe in streaming-proxy returns early 502/504 when the handshake overlaps with the KV migration window.

Priority and impact rationale:
- P1 / Sev1: Dedicated customer-facing regression impacting user experience and risking churn if not mitigated.

Immediate mitigation steps performed:
- Rolled back router prefetch toggle for NimbusApps to false at 2026-03-10 04:30 UTC (confirmed by router logs).
- Deployed a patch to serving runtime to avoid synchronous KV rehydrate on the critical token-emission path as an opt-in flag for affected clusters (canary) at 2026-03-11 01:10 UTC.
- Applied temporary client-side guidance to increase streaming handshake timeout to 10s.

Customer-visible workaround:
- Advised customer to pin to q4 fallback model variant redwood/gptx-7b-v2-int8-fallback (no ABI migration) or keep pre-upgrade runtime (if feasible) until fix is verified.

Next steps / action items:
- Eng (runtime): confirm whether KV migration can be made async or parallel to token emission; PR #582 is the current branch. (Owner: Rafael Costa).
- Eng (router): audit prefetch/warmup path for serialized RPCs; consider making warmup parallel or no-op for pinned customers. (Owner: Priya Shah).
- SRE: run extended canary for patched runtime across 48h on one dedicated cluster and monitor first_token_latency and 5xx rate. (Owner: Marcus Nguyen).
- CS: follow up with NimbusApps with ETA and temporary credit offer; collect additional logs if any more 5xx occur. (Owner: Aisha Patel).

Resolution notes (ongoing):
- 2026-03-11 01:10 UTC: Opt-in async-kv flag deployed to nimbus-dedicated-01; immediate median first_token latency improved to ~220ms in canary traffic.
- 2026-03-11 04:00 UTC: Router prefetch rollback confirmed; some additional improvement in p95 observed.
- Monitoring: canary shows p50 ~240ms, p95 ~380ms, 5xx rate back to baseline for canary flows.
- Full cluster rollout pending completion of integration tests for async-KV path and router warmup changes.

Follow-up / retrospective items:
- Add automated test for ABI migrations that simulates KV rehydrate and asserts token emission is not blocked.
- Update runtime upgrade runbook to include a staged ABI migration and telemetry to flag synchronous rehydrates.
- Improve observability: add a span/tag for 'kv_rehydrate_sync' to quickly correlate with TTFB spikes.
